findings.title: Holdout launcher calls the freeze kit's private git helpers _ls_tree and _cat_blobs
findings.problem: `materialize_plugin_from_candidate` lives in the holdout kit but calls `freeze_common._ls_tree` and `freeze_common._cat_blobs`, both underscore-private helpers of a different kit. The freeze kit's public helpers are `tree_files_at` and `blob_at`, and neither returns blob bytes for a whole tree. So the launcher depends on the freeze kit's internal batch format: the `(mode, kind, oid, path)` tuple order and the `--batch` parser.
findings.current_code:
entries = fcm._ls_tree(repo, sha, PLUGIN_REL)
...
    blobs = fcm._cat_blobs(repo, [oid for _m, _k, oid, _p in entries])
findings.fix_hint: add a public freeze_common helper (e.g. tree_blobs_at(repo, rev, prefix) -> {rel: (mode, bytes)}) and have the launcher call that
findings.why_it_matters: Any refactor of freeze_common's private tuple order or parser breaks the holdout measurement launcher. A change to freeze-kit tools also counts as engineering+detection+workflow under PATH-MAP, so the breakage would only show up as a new candidate and a full rerun.

findings.title: freeze_tally drives score43 through its private _require_complete and _cmd_dev_tally
findings.problem: freeze_tally is the one gate in front of every release tally, and it lives in docs/design. It calls `score43._require_complete(ledger)` and `score43._cmd_dev_tally(view, require_fingerprint=want)`, which are underscore-private internals of a plugin script. `b3-aggregate` goes through the public `score43.run([...])`, but the completeness gate and dev-tally bypass it. pending: confirm score43 has no public equivalent of these two functions (score43.py was not readable from this lane).
findings.fix_hint: expose public score43 entry points (e.g. require_complete, dev_tally) or route through score43.run([...]) with an argv
findings.why_it_matters: A private rename in score43 silently breaks the release-gate tally path. The freeze README names this as the only path that may count runs.

findings.title: freeze_check reaches into eight freeze_manifest private names for its collectors

intent_doc_match.quote: observes the LIVE environment with the same collector functions `freeze_manifest.generate` used

findings.problem: Sharing the collectors with generate is deliberate. But it is done through underscore-private names: `fm._native_cli`, `fm._codex`, `fm._gateway`, `fm._harness_runtime`, `fm._env_value_problem`, `fm._covered_excluded`, `fm._VERSION_RE` and `fm._MODEL_RE`. freeze_tally does the same with `freeze_policy._slot_key`. These collectors are the real contract between the manifest generator and the identity check, yet nothing marks them as public.
findings.current_code:
got = fm._native_cli(live["home"], live["repo"])
...
    got = fm._codex(live["home"], live["codex_home"], live["repo"],
                    manifest["candidate_sha"])
findings.fix_hint: promote the shared collectors to public names (or a small freeze_collect module) so the generator/check contract is explicit
findings.why_it_matters: The identity check is only sound if it observes exactly what the generator recorded. With private naming, nothing signals that editing these helpers changes the identity contract.

findings.title: Third implementation of building the plugin copy from the candidate commit, with diverging rules

intent_doc_match.quote: Every runner materializes its plugin copy from the candidate commit via git (`git archive` or a worktree at the candidate), never from the working tree.

findings.problem: The diff writes the same operation three times. (1) common.sh `b3_materialize_runner` uses `git archive | tar -x`. (2) harness_sandbox.py `snapshot_plugin_from_commit` has its own `_tree_entries` and a second `_cat_blobs` parser (freeze_common already has one). (3) holdout_eval_launch.py `materialize_plugin_from_candidate` uses freeze_common's private helpers. The copies already behave differently: the harness and holdout copies refuse symlinks and keep only 100644/100755, while the B3 tar extraction accepts symlinks. The holdout docstring also claims 'no export attribute can alter it', a property the B3 git-archive path does not have (no .gitattributes is tracked today).
findings.fix_hint: one public freeze_common materializer (ls-tree + cat-file, regular files only) used by the harness and the holdout launcher, with B3 calling it via python3 instead of git archive
findings.why_it_matters: Three runners produce the measured copy under three slightly different rules. A future .gitattributes or symlink in plugins/vibe-check would change only the B3 copy, and the identity check would then refuse B3 alone.

findings.title: Inheritance fields for detection gates leave out the gateway and process env the identity check binds

intent_doc_match.quote: for B3 and holdout, the plugin tree, models, Codex, and the runner's CLI, user level and launch model

findings.problem: What each runner loads is listed twice, and the two lists disagree. `freeze_check.PROFILE_CLASSES['b3']` binds `gateway` and `process_env`, but `GATE_FIELDS['b3x3']` and `GATE_FIELDS['holdoutx3']` include neither. The shared process-env baseline is stored under `runners.fix-harness.env` (`_process_env_baseline`), so a process-env change blocks inheritance only for the workflow gate (`runners.fix-harness`). B3 and holdout results inherit across a manifest whose gateway tree or allowlisted model env (e.g. ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL) changed. pending: owner intent on whether a gateway or env change should force detection reruns.
findings.fix_hint: derive GATE_FIELDS from PROFILE_CLASSES (or add runners.b3.gateway and a top-level process-env field) and move the env baseline out of the fix-harness profile
findings.why_it_matters: Model routing (gateway, env model overrides) can change detection outcomes. Under the current fields those changes do not force detection reruns, while the workflow gate, which they matter less to, is forced to rerun.

findings.title: Holdout launcher adds update pins to the process env checked against a baseline that may lack them
findings.problem: `session_environment` adds `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1` and `DISABLE_UPDATES=1` to the env passed to `verify(..., env=session_env)`. Both keys are in `fm.ENV_ALLOWLIST`, so `_check_process_env` compares them to the manifest baseline, and that baseline is the generator's raw `os.environ` projection. The B3 and fix-harness runners put these pins in settings `env`, not the process env, so only holdout-eval differs here. The launcher's tests mock `verify`, and the live validation command runs the CLI on plain `os.environ`, so neither would catch it. pending: whether FREEZE-MANIFEST was generated with both variables exported in the shell.
findings.fix_hint: pin updates through the materialized settings env (as B3/harness do) or have the process-env check use a per-runner baseline
findings.why_it_matters: If the baseline lacks the pins, every Phase-55 holdout launch stops with 'setting differs: env.DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER', and this would first show up live.

findings.title: Launcher finds freeze_check only through holdout_autopilot's import-time sys.path change
findings.problem: holdout_eval_launch imports holdout_autopilot with the comment '(puts the freeze kit on sys.path)' and then imports freeze_check. The dependency is only an import side effect: holdout_autopilot appends FREEZE_TOOLS to sys.path at module load. Because it uses `append`, any other `freeze_check` or `freeze_common` earlier on the path wins. holdout_autopilot (part of the hashed holdout kit) now also takes a module-level dependency on the freeze kit.
findings.fix_hint: resolve the freeze tools dir explicitly in the launcher (sys.path.insert(0, ...)) instead of relying on autopilot's import side effect
findings.why_it_matters: Reordering or trimming imports in either holdout module silently disables the launcher's identity check path, and it fails closed only at runtime.

findings.title: Update-pin constant defined in four places
findings.problem: `{"DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER": "1", "DISABLE_UPDATES": "1"}` is defined separately in freeze_manifest.UPDATES_EXPECTED, harness_sandbox.SESSION_ENV_PINS, holdout_eval_launch.SESSION_ENV_PINS and b3-runner-v2.12/settings-measured.json `env`. No test locks them equal.
findings.fix_hint: reference freeze_manifest.UPDATES_EXPECTED (or lock the copies equal in a test)
findings.why_it_matters: If a new pin is added in one runner only, the runners stop sharing one update-freeze rule.

findings.title: Covered-path list kept in three places: COVERED, B3_COVERED_KEYS and PATH-MAP
findings.problem: The set of covered paths is written out in freeze_manifest.COVERED, in freeze_check.B3_COVERED_KEYS (B3 and holdout-eval live compare) and as PATH-MAP rules. Tests pin individual entries (runbook, runner inputs) but not set-equality. repo_state step 4 compares every COVERED key at HEAD, which limits the damage. pending: confirm no test asserts that every COVERED entry has a non-reporting PATH-MAP rule.
findings.fix_hint: derive B3_COVERED_KEYS from fm.COVERED by a filter, and add a test that every COVERED key classifies to a rerun category
findings.why_it_matters: The B3 README already says a new runbook must be added to both COVERED and PATH-MAP. Forgetting the third list weakens only the live working-tree comparison.

agent_notes: No import cycle is introduced. Edges: freeze_manifest/check/policy/tally/semgrep_replica -> freeze_common; freeze_check -> freeze_manifest and freeze_policy; freeze_tally -> freeze_policy (+ score43 loaded lazily); harness_sandbox -> freeze_check (lazy); holdout_autopilot and holdout_eval_launch -> freeze_check/freeze_common. The freeze kit never imports harness or holdout code; it only names their paths as data.

freeze_policy copies score43's B3_DIFFS/CATCH_DIFFS/QUIET_EXCLUDED/RUN_NUMBERS on purpose so it never imports score43, and test_freeze_policy locks the copies equal. freeze_manifest.RUNTIME_ROOTS is locked equal to score43 the same way. Both are fine.

freeze_policy.CASE_ID_RE and SEAL_RELPATH copy the holdout kit's id pattern and seal path, with a comment but no lock against holdout_kit.ID_RE that I found. This is a second copy, so below the rule of three; a test lock would be cheap.

Second copies, not findings: manifest discovery and loading exist in freeze_check (active_manifest, load_manifest) and again in freeze_tally._active_manifest_path plus freeze_policy (load_manifest_file, manifest_content_id, which duplicates freeze_manifest.manifest_id). The quoted-token regex exists in freeze_manifest._TOKEN_RE and freeze_check._SCRIPT_TOKEN_RE.

holdout_eval_launch's RUNNER_TEMPLATE/RUNNER_STATUSLINE/placeholder copies are locked equal to freeze_manifest by test_reused_constants, which is good. STRIPPED_ENV and FORBIDDEN_ARGS are shared by identity with the autopilot, which is consistent.

Plugin side (area6): review_archive.py follows the existing small-script pattern (stdlib, argparse with a fail-closed _Parser, exit 0/1/2, import-set test). It replaces the bare mv lines in 90-finalize.md, and test_carry_writers adds it to the archive writer family. score.py's _nv_value/_nv_marked placeholder rule is local and matches the schema/scoring docs. No architectural concerns.

fix-harness changes follow the harness's existing patterns: lazy freeze_check import so the sandbox stays testable without the kit, preflight returning problems, FORMAT_SUBDIR locked to statepath.FORMAT_SUBDIR. The harness, holdout and B3 runners all call the shared freeze_check.verify, matching the owner's 'identity check in every runner' decision.
The .in_use exclusion fix (freeze_common EXCLUDED_NAMES applied to directories too) is in the one shared walker, so every live-tree hash gets it. This is good centralization.
